messages.author: b3ddfbfec9d90e85
messages.subject: Problem getting started with stan
parts:
I have been using rstan for several weeks with no problem. I decided to try using stan so I could use multiple cores when processing large data sets. I have run into a problem running the bernoulli example as explained in the Getting Started section of the stan reference. I have tried this on two computers, both with Windows 7. One already had rstan, R, and rtools installed a few weeks ago The other had never seen any of those and R and rtools were installed immediately before installing stan. After unpacking and building stan with no problems, I ran the command
make src/models/basic_estimators/bernoulli
and during linking got the error message  that is documented in the attached file. Not having looked at C++ since the mid '80's, I have a lot of trouble following all the messages but the problem seems to be
undefined reference to `WinMain@16' 
I did a web search for what might raise error that but didn't find anything with a cause I could address.
My version of make is 3.79.1 and my version of g++ is 4.6.3.
I strongly suspect I've done something silly, but I'm stuck. Thank you for any help you can provide.
Francis C. Costero

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem getting started with stan
parts:
Sorry about that -- it's a known issue that will be patched with the next release: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/338.

Until it's patched, you'll have to specify the executable to build with the full name including file extension. For the bernoulli model, it's:
make src/models/basic_estimators/bernoulli.exe

I've already created a fix for it, but it hasn't been merged into the develop branch yet. That will happen soon.

Once again, sorry about that issue. Hopefully that's clear and you can start using Stan from the command-line.


Daniel
